items.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016
items.q: my partner Carolyn keeps telling me I should write a book.

ctx.x: We’ll lighten it up a little bit. The other day when we were chatting I heard the term “dangling carrot.”

Oh man, the dangling carrot. Well we were talking about — my partner Carolyn keeps telling me I should write a book. And about as far as I’ve gotten on the book is coming up with the title which I thought was The Dangling Carrot which is kind of funny because sometimes in the music business it seems like you’re just about there, you’re just about there and you’re going to snap down on this carrot, whatever the carrot might be, and oops, it’s over there. But fortunately for me I got to take a few chunks out of the…

Well I was a bit surprised when I started doing these interviews that some of the veteran musicians, who we may have this, the way we think about them is oh, they have it made, they’ve had their career and they can choose their gigs. Yet those guys were still scrambling. Like “Bring me to your college.” They were constantly seeking the next gig. And, but wait, you played with Basie and you played with Ellington. Yeah, but that was 30 years ago.
